description: Reorders the channels of a polyphonic cable and can cut the result to fewer channels than came in

params.text: Alt mode: each output channel is drawn at random from the input, so a channel can appear twice or not at all; with it off every input channel appears exactly once

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V draws a new ordering
The channels to be reordered; with nothing patched the module uses twelve channels of a chromatic scale rising from 0V in twelfth-of-a-volt steps
Sets the random seed used at the next trigger, so the same voltage always gives the same ordering; with nothing patched every trigger takes an unpredictable seed
Sets how many channels come out, one channel at 0V and as many as came in at 10V

outputs.text: The input channels in the current order, cut to the channel count set by the Channels input

notes: the drawing between the jacks shows the current ordering: a dot per input channel on the left, a dot per output channel on the right, and a line for each channel that reaches the output.
the ordering is also redrawn whenever the number of input channels changes or the alt mode switch is flipped, reusing the seed of the last trigger rather than drawing a new one.

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1:
continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads a 12-channel chromatic scale.
inputs.2:
±10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads an unpredictable seed each trigger.
inputs.3:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads all the input channels; a negative voltage does nothing here.
